s: An application uses CloudFront, App Runner, and two S3 buckets — one for static assets and one for user-uploaded content. User content is infrequently accessed after 30 days. Users are located only in Europe. How can the company optimize cost?
o: Transition S3 content to Glacier Deep Archive after 30 days.
Use Spot Instances with App Runner.
Add auto scaling to Aurora read replica.
Use CloudFront Price Class 200(Europe and U.S. only).
e: B: Archiving inactive user uploads to Glacier Deep Archive offers the lowest storage cost. E: Since the users are in Europe only, usingPrice Class 200 reduces CloudFront delivery cost without affecting performance. A (expiration) deletes data — not suitable. C is invalid (App Runner does not support Spot). D might save little unless read traffic is high. Reference:CloudFront Price Classes

w.y: The deciding words are "infrequently accessed after 30 days" and "users only in Europe". Moving old uploads to a cheaper S3 storage class and limiting CloudFront to a cheaper price class are the only cost cuts that keep the service working; this dump's wording is rough (Deep Archive has hours of retrieval time, and Price Class 100 is the cheapest one that covers Europe), but B and E are the only workable options.

o.A: Wrong: expiring deletes user content that is still needed.
o.B: Correct: moving rarely read uploads to a colder storage class after 30 days cuts storage cost (Standard-IA would be safer if users still open them).
o.C: Wrong: App Runner does not support Spot capacity.
o.D: Wrong: the architecture has no Aurora, and adding replicas adds cost.
o.E: Correct: a lower CloudFront price class drops expensive edge locations that European users do not need.
